subject: Onsite workshop travel — split charges on corporate card and missing transit receipts
messages:
From: Samantha Mills <samantha@enterpriseinc.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Enterprise Travel Desk <travel@enterpriseinc.com>, Mike Jordan <mike.jordan@enterpriseinc.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Onsite travel charges — help reconciling two ground charges

Hi Connor / Ben —

Thanks again for hosting last week's onsite in SF. Quick one from our travel desk: on 2026-04-15 several of our attendees were billed to Redwood's corporate card for airport transfers, but the charges split oddly across vendors and one attendee's digital receipt is missing. Summary below: 

- Attendee: Mike Jordan (mike.jordan@enterpriseinc.com)
- Expected charge: GroundLink transfer (one consolidated charge)
- Charges observed on Redwood card: GroundLink $1,240.00 (posted 04/15) AND a separate RideShare charge $312.45 (posted 04/15) 
- Missing: digital ride receipt from GroundLink for reconciliation (Travel Desk only has the card transaction)

Can you confirm whether Redwood's travel forwarding or the local vendor split the charge? Our procurement needs a clear audit path (vendor invoice + passenger receipt) to finalize billing. I attached the draft itinerary and the transaction lines we see on the card.

If this needs to be split back to the attendee as a personal expense, please confirm the approach — their travel policy allows for exceptions but requires managerial approval for any reimbursement of personal charges. Hoping we can avoid a manual chargeback.

Thanks —
Samantha
Enterprise Travel Desk
Samantha.Mills@enterpriseinc.com

Attachments: itinerary_Redwood_Enterprise_0415.pdf; cc_statement_0415.pdf

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Mills <samantha@enterpriseinc.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 18 Apr 2026 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Onsite travel charges — help reconciling two ground charges

Hi Samantha —

Appreciate the heads-up and the attachments. I pulled the Redwood corporate card feed and can see the two lines you mentioned. A couple quick notes/questions: 

- We forwarded the airport transfer to GroundLink as a block booking for 8 passengers. GroundLink typically posts a single gross invoice; the RideShare line looks like a fallback when one passenger booked a last-mile ride individually.
- Can you confirm whether Mike used a company-arranged pickup or booked directly in-app? That will determine if this is a vendor split or an incidental personal charge.
- For now I don't want to force a chargeback without evidence — finance should confirm whether we can absorb the incremental RideShare cost under our guest hospitality budget.

Ben — looping you in for the audit path and whether we can process an internal split (vendor invoice + internal waiver) versus asking the attendee to file an expense. Laura, I may need a one-time exception if finance asks to reimburse the attendee and it exceeds the standard hospitality cap.

I'll attach a quick photo of the GroundLink booking confirmation from our booking portal (coming in next email).

—Connor
Head of Partnerships (onsites)
Redwood Inference

Attachments pending: receipt_GroundLink_0415.pdf

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Samantha Mills <samantha@enterpriseinc.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 18 Apr 2026 13:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Onsite travel charges — help reconciling two ground charges

Connor / Samantha —

Thanks. Uploading our reconciliation checklist for transparency: vendor invoice + card transaction + attendee e-receipt or signed SV (service voucher) are required. If any one of those is missing, procurement flags it and we either: (A) request an exception from leadership to approve without full documentation, or (B) return/charge the amount back to the attendee. 

Given the numbers you sent, two options look reasonable: 

1) GroundLink provides a consolidated invoice for the full pickup. We match the $1,240 on the card and mark RideShare $312.45 as a duplicate/fallback (finance writes it off or requests vendor credit). 

2) If RideShare was a personal top-up (attendee paid in-app without company approval), we ask the attendee to submit an expense and we reimburse only with manager approval. 

Please request the GroundLink invoice first. If GroundLink can't provide the passenger receipt, we need Laura's signoff to grant an exception under the guest hospitality policy (code: HOSP-2026). Laura — can you confirm from a policy perspective whether Redwood will cover the RideShare amount as a one-time courtesy for Enterprise guests? Also tagging process: if approved, Ben will mark code HOSP-2026 and I will flag the spend in the May vendor reconciliation.

Ben Carter
Sr. Finance Manager — Payments & Vendor Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachment: reconciliation_checklist_v2.pdf (see internal portal)

From: Samantha Mills <samantha@enterpriseinc.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 19 Apr 2026 08:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Onsite travel charges — help reconciling two ground charges

Thanks — quick update. I spoke to Mike and he confirmed he took a short rideshare for the last mile after GroundLink dropped the group. He thought that was part of the company arrangement and didn't realize it would post separately. He sent a screenshot of his in-app receipt; attaching here (receipt_GroundLink_0415.pdf). GroundLink also emailed an invoice but it only lists the block booking total; it doesn't enumerate passenger-level microcharges.

If Redwood decides to absorb the $312.45, we can mark it as guest hospitality. Otherwise, Mike can file a small expense report. He prefers Redwood to cover it to avoid friction with the event.

Samantha Mills
Enterprise Travel Desk

Attachments: receipt_GroundLink_0415.pdf

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Samantha Mills <samantha@enterpriseinc.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2026 15:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Onsite travel charges — help reconciling two ground charges

Connor / Ben / Samantha —

Appreciate the context and the receipts. Given this was an invited Enterprise guest and the amount is modest, I approve a one-time hospitality exception to cover the $312.45. Please do the following: 

- Ben: code the payment to expense code HOSP-2026 and note "Guest — Enterprise SF onsite — exception approved by LB" in the vendor reconciliation comments.
- Connor: flag internal playbook (onsite runbook) to remind leads to communicate the boundary between block transfers and individual top-ups. Add a short note to the organizer checklist: "Confirm riders understand whether in-app payments are separate charges."
- Samantha / Mike: if you prefer, we can cancel any expense request — otherwise Mike may leave the receipt for finance reference.

Ben — once posted, please send the journal entry so we can close the ticket. I'll circulate a brief note to growth/ops so they know the exception precedent.

Laura Bennett
VP, Operations & Program Management
Redwood Inference

--
Final: Ben confirms posting and marks ticket INF-2319 closed.
